data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A single evaluation distinguishes genuine reliability gain from mere compliance by testing whether the panel's accuracy degrades gracefully or catastrophically when one checklist item is adversarially perturbed into plausible-but-misleading distractors; a genuine reliability gain implies graceful degradation because the panel internalizes underlying structure, while mere compliance implies cliff-edge collapse when the checklist's surface pattern is subtly broken.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the perturbed checklist item is not the sole pathway to the outcome, but multiple checklist items independently suffice, compliance will degrade gracefully despite no internalization, making the test insensitive.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the expert also fails catastrophically on the perturbed subset due to the same misleading distractor, the test confounds panel structure with expert framing-fragility, yielding no separating evidence.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If the checklist is lossless compression of relevant regularities (per SCR_001), perturbing one item disrupts only the corresponding local regularity. A panel that internalizes the structure compensates using cross-item dependencies, producing graceful degradation. A panel merely tracking surface compliance lacks such dependencies, so perturbing a single item that was the only cue for the correct outcome should collapse accuracy to near-baseline on that subset, because the checklist offered no redundant pathways.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
